originalTitle: China’s Stock Market Is Trailing the U.S. by the Widest Margin in History
summary: The gap between U.S. and Chinese stocks just broke a record stretching back decades, and Beijing's state-backed funds are still sitting on their hands while blue-chip shares slide into bear market territory.
content:
The gap between U.S. and Chinese stocks just broke a record stretching back decades, and Beijing's state-backed funds are still sitting on their hands while blue-chip shares slide into bear market territory.

When trading ended on Thursday, October 22, the S&P 500 closed at 2.095 times the Shanghai Composite. By our calculation from daily closes, that is the highest ratio in the data going back to 1997, exceeding the 2.088 record set on September 19, 2024.

The S&P 500’s ratio to Hong Kong’s Hang Seng also closed at a record 0.334, in data back to 1990. Both ratios fell Friday to 2.066 and 0.330 as Shanghai rallied. Even so, the gap hit the widest margin on record during the week ended October 23.

The ETF also hit a record. Measured in dollars with dividends included, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( NYSEARCA:SPY ) did so against the iShares MSCI China ETF ( NASDAQ:MCHI ) on October 22, in data back to 2011. The index ratios compare price levels in local currency. The fund comparison shows what a U.S. investor actually earned.

Investors must judge whether China is a value trap. It could be a market that looks cheap but keeps falling, or a deep discount that Beijing’s state funds have only started to buy.

Through October 23, the S&P 500 has gained 11.4% in 2026. Over the same stretch, the Shanghai Composite fell 7.0%, and the Hang Seng fell 9.9%.

By our calculation, the S&P 500 is ahead of Shanghai by about 18 percentage points and ahead of MCHI by about 30 points, since MCHI is down 18.4%. The record shows up in the cumulative ratio, which captures years of difference, rather than in any single year.

Thursday’s Selloff Pushed the CSI 300 Into a Bear Market

The CSI 300, China’s blue-chip index, fell 1.8% to 4,036.30, its lowest close since July 2025. It entered a bear market Thursday, finishing 20.2% below its June 22 closing peak. The Shanghai Composite dropped 1.5% to its lowest level in more than a year, and the Hang Seng Tech index hit a two-year low.

Alibaba Group ( NYSE:BABA | BABA Price Prediction ) fell more than 6% and Tencent fell 2.9%. Investors doubted that AI growth and valuations could last. They were let down by Beijing’s incremental stimulus and pulled back after Beijing moved to tax offshore trusts held by shareholders of Hong Kong-listed Chinese companies.

“The market is in the dump,” said Hao Hong, CIO at Lotus Asset Management. He added that the National Team, the state-backed funds that buy shares to steady prices, “has been rather hesitant to make a move.”

State-Backed Buying Produced Only a Partial Rebound

On Friday, heavy trading in ETFs preferred by state-backed investors lifted the CSI 300 1.7% and the Shanghai Composite 0.9%. The CSI 300 still lost 1.6% for the week. That was its 11th straight weekly decline, the longest losing streak since the index was created in 2005, and it ended about 19% below its June peak.

Morgan Stanley analysts spoke. They said, “weak domestic demand and liquidity headwinds persist, while valuations have yet to reach an outright bottom.” The S&P 500 dropped 0.52% Friday, which means the record gap came from China falling while U.S. stocks also dropped.

Internet Stocks Took the Heaviest Losses

The KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF ( NYSEARCA:KWEB ) fell 0.30% Friday to $23.14 and lost about 5.2% for the week. It is down 32.0% in 2026, and its one-year total return is -37.79%, because a fund made up only of internet stocks takes the most damage when AI and tech valuations are the worry.

The iShares China Large-Cap ETF ( NYSEARCA:FXI ), which holds $3.78 billion in assets, fell 0.43% to $32.31. It is down 15.6% in 2026, with a one-year return of -17.20%, because its big banks offset part of the tech losses. MCHI, the widest of the three funds, dropped 0.04% to $49.00, just above its 52-week low of $48.65, and its one-year return is -20.79%.

Bull and Bear Cases for Chinese Stocks at a Record Discount

The bull case rests on price: Chinese shares trade at a record discount to U.S. stocks, and Friday showed that state money will step in when selling turns chaotic.

The bear case rests on earnings, because domestic demand is weak, stimulus keeps arriving in small pieces, and the offshore trust tax adds new policy risk. The National Team also held off until the CSI 300 had already dropped into a bear market.

We side with the bears. A market that keeps getting cheaper stays a value trap until earnings turn, and among the three funds, FXI’s bank-heavy portfolio has held up far better than KWEB.

Two signals would test this view: if the CSI 300 ends its losing streak with a weekly gain and Beijing announces a real fiscal package, the bull case gets stronger. If MCHI closes below $48.65, the bear case is confirmed.

Omor Ibne Ehsan is a writer at 24/7 Wall St. He is a self-taught investor with a focus on growth, cyclical, and dividend equities that have strong fundamentals, value, and long-term potential. He also has an interest in high-risk, high-reward investments such as penny stocks.
chineseTitle: 中国股市落后美国股市历史最大差距
chineseSummary: 美国和中国股市之间的差距刚刚打破了几十年来的纪录，而北京的国家支持基金仍在按兵不动，而蓝筹股却滑入熊市区域。
chineseContent:
美国和中国股市之间的差距刚刚打破了几十年来的纪录，而北京的国家支持基金仍在按兵不动，而蓝筹股却滑入熊市区域。

10 月 22 日星期四交易结束时，标准普尔 500 指数收于上证综指的 2.095 倍。根据我们按日收盘价计算，这是自 1997 年以来数据中的最高比率，超过了 2024 年 9 月 19 日创下的 2.088 纪录。

标准普尔 500 指数与香港恒生指数的比率也收于创纪录的 0.334，数据可追溯至 1990 年。周五，随着上海股市上涨，两个比率均下跌至 2.066 和 0.330。即便如此，截至 10 月 23 日当周，这一差距还是创下了有记录以来的最大差距。

该ETF也创下了历史新高。以包含股息的美元计算，SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) 于 10 月 22 日与 iShares MSCI China ETF (NASDAQ:MCHI) 进行了对比，数据可追溯至 2011 年。指数比率比较以当地货币计算的价格水平。基金比较显示了美国投资者的实际收入。

投资者必须判断中国是否是一个价值陷阱。这可能是一个看似便宜但不断下跌的市场，也可能是北京国家资金刚刚开始买入的大幅折扣。

截至 10 月 23 日，标准普尔 500 指数在 2026 年上涨了 11.4%。同期，上证综指下跌 7.0%，恒生指数下跌 9.9%。

根据我们的计算，标普 500 指数领先上证指数约 18 个百分点，领先 MCHI 约 30 个百分点，因为 MCHI 下跌了 18.4%。该记录以累积比率显示，它捕获了年份的差异，而不是任何单一年份。

周四的抛售将沪深300指数推入熊市

中国蓝筹股指数沪深300指数下跌1.8%，至4,036.30点，为2025年7月以来的最低收盘价。该指数周四进入熊市，较6月22日收盘高点下跌20.2%。上证综合指数下跌1.5%，创一年多以来最低水平，恒生科技指数触及两年来新低。

阿里巴巴集团（NYSE：BABA | BABA 价格预测）下跌超过 6%，腾讯下跌 2.9%。投资者怀疑人工智能的增长和估值能否持续。他们对北京的增量刺激感到失望，并在北京对在香港上市的中国公司股东持有的离岸信托征税后撤回。

“市场正在下跌，”莲花资产管理公司首席信息官洪浩表示。他补充说，国家队，即以稳定价格购买股票的国家支持基金，“对于采取行动一直相当犹豫”。

国家支持的购买仅产生了部分反弹

周五，受国家支持的投资者青睐的 ETF 交易活跃，沪深 300 指数上涨 1.7%，上证综合指数上涨 0.9%。沪深300指数本周仍下跌1.6%。这是该指数连续第 11 周下跌，是该指数自 2005 年创建以来最长的连续下跌趋势，收盘时比 6 月份的峰值低了约 19%。

摩根士丹利分析师发表讲话。他们表示，“国内需求疲软和流动性逆风持续存在，而估值尚未完全触底。”标准普尔 500 指数周五下跌 0.52%，这意味着创纪录的差距来自中国股市下跌，而美国股市也下跌。

互联网股跌幅最大

金瑞CSI中国互联网ETF（NYSEARCA：KWEB）周五下跌0.30%，至23.14美元，本周下跌约5.2%。 2026 年将下跌 32.0%，一年总回报率为-37.79%，因为当人工智能和科技估值令人担忧时，仅由互联网股票组成的基金遭受的损失最大。

持有资产37.8亿美元的iShares中国大盘ETF（NYSEARCA：FXI）下跌0.43%，至32.31美元。 2026年下跌15.6%，一年回报率为-17.20%，因为其大银行抵消了部分科技损失。三只基金中范围最广的MCHI下跌0.04%，至49.00美元，略高于52周低点48.65美元，一年回报率为-20.79%。

中国股票的牛市和熊市案例以创纪录的折价

看涨的理由取决于价格：中国股市的交易价格相对于美国股市有创纪录的折价，周五的情况表明，当抛售变得混乱时，国家资金将介入。

看空的理由取决于盈利，因为国内需求疲软，刺激措施不断小规模实施，而且离岸信托税增加了新的政策风险。国家队也一直等到沪深300已经跌入熊市。

我们站在熊一边。在盈利转向之前，持续变得更便宜的市场仍然是一个价值陷阱，在这三只基金中，FXI 的银行为主的投资组合的表现远远好于 KWEB。

有两个信号可以检验这一观点：如果沪深 300 指数以周度上涨结束连跌，并且北京宣布真正的财政刺激计划，那么牛市的理由就会变得更强。如果 MCHI 收盘价低于 48.65 美元，则熊市情况得到确认。
